title: AWS Account and Environment Setup
description: Create an AWS account, install the AWS CLI, and configure Visual Studio for AWS development.

data.text: Before calling AWS from C#, you need an AWS account, the AWS CLI, and the right tools in Visual Studio or the .NET CLI.

data.title: Account setup steps
items: Go to https://aws.amazon.com and click **Create an AWS account**
Enter your email, password, and account name
Provide contact information and payment method
Verify your identity with a phone call or text message

data.title: Free tier
data.text: AWS Free Tier includes 12 months of popular services like Lambda, S3, and RDS. Always check the Free Tier limits to avoid unexpected charges.
The AWS CLI lets you script AWS operations from PowerShell, Bash, or C# processes.

data.title: Install AWS CLI on Windows with winget
data.content:
Use winget to install the AWS CLI.
# Expected output: "Successfully installed Amazon.AWSCLI"

data.title: Verify installation and configure credentials
data.content:
After installation, open a new terminal and configure your credentials.
# Expected output after --version: "aws-cli/2.x.x Python/3.x.x Windows/10 exe/AMD64 prompt/off"
# aws configure prompts for: AWS Access Key ID, AWS Secret Access Key, Default region, Default output format

items: In Visual Studio Installer, select the **ASP.NET and web development** workload
Install the **AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio** extension from the Visual Studio Marketplace
The AWS Toolkit lets you deploy directly from Visual Studio and manage resources

data.title: Create your first S3 bucket
data.description: Use the AWS CLI to create an S3 bucket and verify it exists.
steps: Run `aws configure` and enter your Access Key ID and Secret Access Key
Run `aws sts get-caller-identity` to confirm authentication
Run `aws s3 ls` to list your buckets
data.expectedOutcome: You see the new bucket listed in the output.

data.title: Environment Checklist
points: AWS account created with verified identity
AWS CLI installed and `aws configure` succeeds
Visual Studio has the AWS Toolkit or .NET CLI is ready
One S3 bucket created for the exercises in this course
data.takeaway: With an account, CLI, and AWS Toolkit, you are ready to provision AWS resources from the command line and from C#.
